Your Trusted Partner in Private Aviation
========================================

About Executive Jet Management

  

For more than 45 years, EJM has simplified private travel by handling the finer details of jet management and charter—so you can focus on the big picture. Whether you are new to private aviation or an experienced aircraft owner, we support your unique travel needs through our safety-first practices, global scale, and continued commitment to world-class service. 

### Then and Now 

Since beginning as American Air Services in 1977, EJM has grown to become the largest aircraft management and charter company in the industry. In 1988, we joined the NetJets portfolio of companies, which was purchased by Berkshire Hathaway a decade later. Today, we facilitate seamless travel for aircraft Owners and charter customers across the U.S. and Europe. 

### All of Us, Serving You

When you join EJM, our team of over 1,000 passionate professionals becomes your team. Some of these experts have spent their entire careers in aviation, while others honed their skills in diverse industries. All bring unique experiences and insights to EJM, which they leverage to perfect your experience and fuel our culture of curiosity, collaboration, adaptability, and integrity.

 Our executive leaders bring decades of experience to EJM, with the majority having spent their entire careers in aviation. Meet the team propelling us forward.

**Brian Hirsh**
---------------

#### **President**

![](https://www.executivejetmanagement.com/cms/delivery/media/UU46n9rA54mHw0Och0IIyO7nBfEouKxVfUGZtibMN.g=)

Brian joined the Executive Jet Management® (EJM) team as president in 2018. He spearheads our relentless safety-first culture, leading a team of world-class aviation professionals who together have grown EJM into the world's largest aircraft management and charter company. Brian's leadership emphasizes that "Because How Matters" is more than just a slogan for EJM—it is the embodiment of our entire team's deep commitment to operating with integrity and doing everything the right way.

  

Prior to leading EJM, Brian was president of QS Partners®, the whole aircraft sales, brokerage, and acquisitions arm of NetJets®, where he oversaw the public launch and expansion of the brand. In over a decade with the NetJets family of brands, Brian has held a variety of leadership roles within operations, sales, finance, and aircraft asset management.

  

A Cincinnati native, Brian holds a bachelor's degree from Duke University in mechanical engineering and a master's degree from Georgia Tech's School of Aerospace Engineering. His aviation career started at GE Aircraft Engines (today known as GE Aviation), where he worked on several commercial and military engine programs.

---------------------

![](https://www.executivejetmanagement.com/cms/delivery/media/UU46n9rA54mHw0Och0IIyO7nBfEouKxVfUGZtibMN.g=)

Mike joined the EJM team in January 2020 following a 10-year career with Jet Aviation in sales leadership roles. His leadership approach focuses on a client-first mentality, building trusted partnerships. Mike's career in aviation spans more than 20 years, including roles in both global commercial airlines and nationally regarded jet brokerage and management firms, leading sales, operations, safety, and management positions.

Mike has a Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater and is based in Chicago. He is an active member in the aviation industry, including participating in the International Aviation Dealers Association and the National Aviation Finance Association.

Executive Jet Management
========================

Touting itself as the “largest aircraft management and charter service in the world,” [NetJets](https://www.bjtonline.com/company/netjets)
 subsidiary Executive Jet Management operates globally, managing more than 230 aircraft and offering air charter service through on-demand and flat-rate programs.    

Former [Cessna](https://www.bjtonline.com/company/cessna)
 Aircraft salesman and demonstration pilot Joseph Moeggenberg founded the company as American Air Services at Lunken Airport in Cincinnati in 1977. Executive Jet Aviation, based in nearby Columbus, Ohio, acquired the company in 1988, changing its name to Executive Jet Management while retaining Moeggenberg as president and CEO. He remained with EJM until 1995, when he left to found Aviation Research Group/US (ARGUS). 

Berkshire Hathaway bought EJM's parent company in 1998, renaming it [NetJets](https://www.bjtonline.com/company/netjets)
 in 2002. That year, EJM reached the 100-aircraft-managed mark. Adding all managed aircraft to its FAA Part 135 charter certificate, the company maintained a fleet of around 100 airplanes until NetJets' Benjamin Murray became EJM president and CEO in 2007. He set goals to double the size of the managed fleet and instituted a program to manage aircraft whose owners didn't want them on a charter certificate. As of February 2021, only 126 of EJM's 236 managed aircraft were on its charter certificate.  

EJM initiated a Support Services program to flight departments and aircraft owners in 2012, offering cost savings on fuel and crew training plus VIP access to FBOs in key cities. Also that year, the company established a regional base in Lisbon, Portugal; and NetJets began a foray into China. By May 2015, EJM was managing 208 aircraft in the U.S., seven in Europe via subsidiary EJM Europe, and two in China under the EJM China brand.  

In January 2019, EJM launched its Ascend flat-rate charter program; a $100,000 deposit guarantees Ascend customers access to any cabin class in the EJM fleet with 24 hours' booking notice. 

In late 2020, EJM opened operations centers in San Jose, California, and Denver for flight operations, fleet maintenance, aircraft management, and charter sales. 

EJM and its employees have received many FAA maintenance awards since 1994, among them 13 Diamond Awards of Excellence and three Charles Taylor Master Mechanic Awards. 

The company manages more than 41,500 flights for 86,000 passengers visiting about 120 countries annually.
